76.name: Alize Red Passion
76.note: Cognac and passion fruit. Sweet, nostalgic for anyone who remembers its 90s/2000s heyday.

147.name: Arrow Creme De Cacao Brown
147.note: A budget creme de cacao. Thinner than Marie Brizard, but functional in a mixed drink.

148.name: Arrow Creme De Cacao White
148.note: Same budget tier as the brown version, clear rather than colored.

154.name: Arrow Peach Schnapps
154.note: Rock-bottom peach schnapps. Purely a mixer.

166.name: Asbach Uralt Brandy
166.note: German brandy, dry and oaky. More restrained than the sweet French entry-level brandies.

195.name: Bacardi Bahama Mama
195.note: Sweet party-jug tiki drink. Not much rum character, but cheap and does the job for a group.

293.name: Barton Gin
293.note: Bottom shelf and tastes it. Mixer of last resort.

358.name: Black Haus Blackberry Schnapps
358.note: German import, real blackberry character instead of candy syrup. A cut above the domestic fruit schnapps.

362.name: Black Velvet Portable
362.note: Rock-bottom Canadian whisky. Buy it for the price, not the flavor.

402.name: Bombay Sapphire Gin
402.note: Vapor-infused and gentle. Famous, but Bombay Dry has more character for less.

406.name: Boodles Gin
406.note: No citrus botanicals at all — pure juniper, nutmeg, sage. A martini gin.

408.name: Booker's Bourbon
408.note: Jim Beam's uncut, unfiltered flagship. Big, oaky, and one of the more consistent barrel-proof bourbons on the market.

440.name: Branca Menta
440.note: Mint version of Fernet-Branca. Cooling and intensely herbal — a love-it-or-hate-it digestif.

447.name: Broker's Gin
447.note: The value pick of the whole list. 94 proof, proper juniper, eighteen dollars.

453.name: Buffalo Trace Bourbon
453.note: The reference point for what bourbon should cost and taste like. Grab it when you see it.

454.name: Bulleit Bourbon
454.note: High-rye mashbill, spicier than most bourbons at this price. Reliable well pour.

471.name: Burnett's Vodka
471.note: Cheap and neutral. Better than the true bottom shelf, still just a mixer.

514.name: Campari Aperitivo
514.note: Bitter orange, unmistakable. Half of a negroni and most of a spritz.

611.name: Chartreuse Yellow
611.note: Softer, sweeter, honeyed. The approachable Chartreuse — and increasingly scarce.

662.name: Chopin Vodka
662.note: Potato-based, creamy texture. Distinctive, and thirty dollars.

686.name: Citadelle Gin
686.note: French, nineteen botanicals, floral but the juniper still shows up. Versatile.

716.name: Cointreau
716.note: The orange liqueur worth the money. Cleaner and drier than triple sec.

796.name: Cruzan Dark Rum
796.note: A little molasses depth. Fine for cooking and dark-and-stormies.

822.name: Cynar
822.note: Artichoke amaro. Odd on paper, excellent in a drink.

864.name: Dekuyper Blue Curacao
864.note: Mostly food coloring and orange flavor. Fun for a blue drink, nothing more.

901.name: Dekuyper Peachtree Schnapps
901.note: The standard peach schnapps. Genuinely useful in a Sex on the Beach, not just a shot.

903.name: Dekuyper Peppermint Schnapps
903.note: Classic hot cocoa and peppermint patty mixer. Nothing fancy, does the job.

912.name: Dekuyper Sour Apple Pucker Schnapps
912.note: The Appletini building block. Artificial but convincingly sour-apple.

920.name: Dekuyper Watermelon Pucker Schnapps
920.note: Sour watermelon candy. Interchangeable with the rest of the Pucker line.

1000.name: Dr. Mcgillcuddy's Vanilla
1000.note: Smooth vanilla, works in coffee drinks. Better as a mixer than a shot.

1001.name: Drambuie
1001.note: Honeyed scotch liqueur. A rusty nail and not much else.

1048.name: Elmer T Lee Bourbon
1048.note: A Buffalo Trace classic, named for the man who created the modern single-barrel category. Excellent, though the price here reflects real scarcity.

1125.name: Frangelico
1125.note: Hazelnut, in the monk-shaped bottle. Pleasant.

1273.name: Grand Marnier
1273.note: Cognac-based orange. Richer than Cointreau, sweeter too.

1304.name: Grey Goose Le Citron Vodka
1304.note: Bright, genuine lemon flavor on an excellent base spirit.

1305.name: Grey Goose Vodka
1305.note: Soft and clean. You are paying for the marketing.

1362.name: Herradura Anejo Tequila
1362.note: A classic, dependable anejo. Oak and vanilla without losing the agave underneath.

1621.name: Jagermeister
1621.note: The German herbal digestif everyone's tried as a shot. Polarizing, but a genuine flavor, not neutral spirit.

1692.name: Johnnie Walker Gold
1692.note: Smoother and more refined than Black, with real Speyside character coming through.

1760.name: Kamora Coffee
1760.note: A budget Kahlua alternative. Thinner but does the job in a White Russian.

1929.name: Luksusowa Vodka
1929.note: Polish potato vodka. More body and character than the wheat vodkas twice its price.

1958.name: Maker's Mark Bourbon
1958.note: The red wax bottle. Soft, sweet, wheated — reliably good and always in stock.

1982.name: Marie Brizard Apry
1982.note: Apricot liqueur from a respected French house. Real fruit character, useful in classic cocktails.

1986.name: Marie Brizard Parfait Amour
1986.note: A floral, violet-tinged curacao variant. More of a novelty than a workhorse liqueur.

2018.name: Massenez Creme De Cassis De Dijon
2018.note: French blackcurrant liqueur, real depth. What a kir royale should actually taste like.

2088.name: Metaxa Ouzo
2088.note: A reliable Greek ouzo, anise-forward and traditional.

2102.name: Midori Melon
2102.note: Bright green melon liqueur. A novelty mixer more than a sipper.

2107.name: Milagro Select Barrel Reserve Reposado Tequila
2107.note: Milagro's step up from their standard reposado. Well-balanced and food-friendly.

2130.name: Monte Alban Mezcal
2130.note: The one with the worm. A novelty, not a mezcal.

2204.name: Nonino Quintessentia Amaro
2204.note: Orange and caramel, beautifully balanced. The gateway amaro.

2265.name: Old Grand Dad 80
2265.note: The 80-proof version. Fine, but the 100 is two dollars more and much better.

2266.name: Old Grand Dad 100
2266.note: Bonded, high-rye, twenty-five dollars. The thinking person’s cheap bourbon.

2267.name: Old Grand Dad 114
2267.note: High-rye and 114 proof for thirty dollars. Spicy, hot, excellent in an old fashioned.

2281.name: Old Overholt
2281.note: The 80-proof version. Get the bonded instead.

2320.name: Ouzo 12
2320.note: Greek anise spirit. Turns milky over ice, classic with seafood.

2389.name: Pig Nose Scotch
2389.note: Marketed as "smooth as a pig's nose." Light, easy-drinking, a decent value blend.

2391.name: Pimm's No. 1 Cup
2391.note: British gin-based fruit cup. Made for a Pimm's Cup on a summer afternoon, little use otherwise.

2398.name: Plymouth Gin
2398.note: Earthier and less juniper-forward than a London dry. Its own protected style, worth trying once.

2514.name: Rhum Barbancourt 5 Star Reserve Speciale
2514.note: More aged and refined than the 3 Star, with the same distinctive cane-juice character.

2574.name: Rumple Minze
2574.note: 100 proof peppermint, ice-cold out of the freezer. The one schnapps most people actually ask for by name.

2581.name: Ryan's Cream
2581.note: A bottom-shelf Irish cream. Thin compared to Carolans, but cheap.

2659.name: Seagram's Extra Smooth Vodka
2659.note: A basic, inoffensive value vodka. Buy it for the price.

2724.name: Smirnoff Citrus Vodka
2724.note: Straightforward citrus, interchangeable with the rest of the Smirnoff flavor line.

2878.name: Talisker Single Malt
2878.note: The 10-year. Peppery, coastal, half-smoked. A very good middle path.

2891.name: Tanqueray No. 10
2891.note: Tanqueray's top shelf, whole fresh citrus in the still. Noticeably better than the standard bottle.

2967.name: Three Olives Vodka
2967.note: A clean, unremarkable everyday vodka. Slightly smoother than the bottom-shelf brands.

3073.name: Virginia Gentleman
3073.note: The Virginia standby. Sentimental value exceeds flavor value.

3175.name: Yukon Jack
3175.note: Whisky-based honey liqueur. Sweet and simple, a dated party staple.

3218.name: Effen Vodka
3218.note: French wheat vodka, a bit sweeter than most. Solid, unremarkable.

3248.name: Woodford Reserve Bourbon
3248.note: The default "nicer" bourbon at a bar. Well balanced, a fair step up from the well pours above.

3250.name: Milagro Silver Tequila
3250.note: Clean but a touch thin for thirty-seven dollars.

3318.name: Absolut Vodka
3318.note: Perfectly good, faintly sweet. The default.

3325.name: Aristocrat Vodka
3325.note: Rock-bottom vodka. Buy it for the price.

3357.name: Christian Brothers Brandy
3357.note: Cheap American brandy. A mixer, not a sipper.

3365.name: Evan Williams Egg Nog
3365.note: A genuine bourbon-based egg nog rather than a neutral-spirit one. The best-known name in the category for a reason.

3379.name: Glenfiddich Solera Reserve Single Malt
3379.note: Matured using a solera system for consistency. Rich and well-regarded.

3393.name: Hendrick's Gin
3393.note: Cucumber and rose. The gin that convinced a generation gin was not just juniper.

3431.name: Pampero Aniversary Rum
3431.note: Venezuelan, comes in a leather-wrapped bottle. Smooth and traditional, priced fairly for the presentation.

3445.name: Skyy Vodka
3445.note: Clean and neutral. A step up from the bottom shelf, nothing more.

3451.name: Tanqueray Gin
3451.note: Four botanicals, 94.6 proof, nothing wasted. The one to beat under thirty dollars.

3565.name: Pinnacle Vodka
3565.note: A clean, budget-friendly everyday vodka. Nothing remarkable, nothing wrong with it.

3571.name: Aristocrat Peach Schnapps
3571.note: Bottom-shelf jug schnapps. Buy it for the price and nothing else.

3589.name: Caravella Limoncello
3589.note: Italian lemon liqueur, bright and sweet. A good summer sipper, chilled.

3733.name: Van Gogh Citroen Vodka
3733.note: Bright citrus, a well-made flavored vodka in the same tier as Ketel One Citroen.

3773.name: Stolichnaya Elit
3773.note: Stoli's flagship, freeze-filtered. The best version of a brand mostly known for its cheap flavored line.

3866.name: Zaya Rum
3866.note: Trinidad blend, smooth and a little vanilla-sweet. A good gift bottle.

3873.name: Jose Cuervo Golden Margarita
3873.note: The bottled-margarita default at every gas station. Thin tequila flavor, mostly sour mix.

3923.name: Talisker Distiller's Edition
3923.note: Amoroso sherry-finished. Rich, peppery, and one of the best regarded Talisker expressions.

3924.name: Dalwhinnie Distiller's Edition
3924.note: A sherry-finished variant, richer than the standard 15 Year.

3925.name: Glenkinchie Distiller's Edition
3925.note: Amontillado-finished, slightly richer than the standard 12 Year Lowland malt.

4025.name: Marie Brizard Triple Sec
4025.note: A genuinely good triple sec, a real step up from Bols or Arrow for margaritas and sidecars.

4026.name: Marie Brizard Blackberry Liqueur
4026.note: Solid blackberry flavor, a step up from the domestic mass brands.

4046.name: Van Gogh Double Espresso Vodka
4046.note: Genuine espresso character, one of the better coffee-flavored vodkas.

4069.name: PAMA Pomegranate
4069.note: Real pomegranate character, tart rather than syrupy. Versatile in cocktails.

4125.name: Ramazzotti Amaro
4125.note: Classic Italian amaro, slightly sweeter and syrupy. A good introduction to the category.

4136.name: Pallini Raspicello Liqueur
4136.note: Raspberry variant, consistent with the quality of their limoncello.

4137.name: Pallini Peachcello Liqueur
4137.note: The Pallini formula applied to peach. Well-made, less iconic than their limoncello.

4154.name: Seagram's Distiller's Reserve Gin
4154.note: A real step up from standard Seagram's for two dollars more.

4189.name: Trader Vic's Kona Coffee Liqueur
4189.note: Real Kona coffee character, a step up from the mass-market coffee liqueurs.

4206.name: Catdaddy Carolina Moonshine
4206.note: Spiced with cinnamon and vanilla rather than fruit — one of the more distinctive shines here.

4461.name: Aperol
4461.note: Gentler and sweeter than Campari. The spritz bottle.

4532.name: Wild Turkey American Honey
4532.note: Honey liqueur at 71 proof. Sweet, and not really whiskey any more.

4537.name: Smirnoff Orange Vodka
4537.note: Basic orange flavor, does the job in a screwdriver.

4570.name: Grey Goose La Poire Vodka
4570.note: Pear flavor, subtle and well-integrated rather than candy-sweet.

4664.name: X-Rated Fusion
4664.note: Vodka, mango, and passion fruit. Sweet, built for shots and mixed drinks.

4671.name: Dr. McGuillicuddy's Cherry Schnapps
4671.note: Cough-syrup cherry, but that is exactly the appeal at a shot bar.

4737.name: Bluecoat Gin
4737.note: Philadelphia, 94 proof, big organic citrus. Assertive.

4902.name: Lagavulin Distillers Edition
4902.note: Pedro Ximenez sherry-finished. One of the most acclaimed Islay expressions available.

4964.name: St. Germain Liqueur
4964.note: Elderflower — floral and versatile. Easy to overuse.

5078.name: E & J VSOP Brandy
5078.note: A small step above E&J VS. Still mostly a well pour.

5084.name: Hennessy VS
5084.note: The standard. Fruity, a bit hot, very consistent.

5094.name: Glenmorangie Quinta Ruban Scotch
5094.note: Port-cask finished, richer and fruitier than the Original. A well-regarded step up.

5095.name: Glenmorangie Lasanta Scotch
5095.note: Sherry-finished, nutty and sweet. A good step past the entry level.

5098.name: Arrow Peppermint Schnapps
5098.note: A budget stand-in for Rumple Minze. Thinner, but cheap by the handle.

5167.name: New Amsterdam Straight Gin
5167.note: Almost no juniper — closer to citrus vodka. Popular, not good.

5197.name: Hangar One Vodka
5197.note: American craft vodka, grape-and-grain blend. Smooth, well-regarded among craft options.

5208.name: Prairie Organic Vodka
5208.note: Organic corn vodka, smooth and neutral. Solid everyday choice.

5255.name: Domaine De Canton
5255.note: French ginger liqueur, real ginger heat and depth. Excellent in cocktails.

5608.name: Crop Organic Cucumber Vodka
5608.note: Genuine organic cucumber character, refreshing and well-made.

5693.name: Captain Morgan Long Island Iced Tea
5693.note: A basic party-jug Long Island, more sweet than boozy-tasting.

5698.name: Jose Cuervo Authentic Mango Margarita
5698.note: Sweet and fruity, tequila character is an afterthought.

5736.name: Four Roses Single Barrel Bourbon
5736.note: One recipe, one barrel, more intense than the Small Batch. The better bottle if you can spend a bit more.

5737.name: Four Roses Small Batch Bourbon
5737.note: Four of the ten Four Roses recipes blended. Fruity and spicy — excellent for the price.

5738.name: Four Roses Bourbon
5738.note: The yellow label. Light, floral, forgiving — good for someone new to bourbon.

5751.name: Dewar's 18 YR Founders Reserve
5751.note: Rich and complex for a blend, one of the better-aged Dewar's expressions.

5772.name: Skyy Infusions Pineapple
5772.note: Tropical and genuine-tasting, solid mid-tier flavored vodka.

5800.name: Sailor Jerry Spiced Rum
5800.note: Spicier and less candied than Captain Morgan. The better spiced rum for nearly the same money.

5843.name: The Scarlet Ibis Rum
5843.note: Trinidadian, made for classic tiki cocktails. A fair Angostura-adjacent choice.

5854.name: DeKuyper Island Punch Pucker
5854.note: Generic tropical-punch sweetness. Fine as a mixer, unremarkable neat.

5963.name: Wild Turkey 101 Rye
5963.note: 101 proof and full of baking spice. A manhattan built for it.

6165.name: Mekhong Spirit Of Thailand
6165.note: A rice-and-sugarcane Thai spirit, herbal and unusual for a domestic shelf. Interesting more than essential.

6169.name: Jim Beam Bourbon
6169.note: The white label. It is everywhere for a reason, and that reason is not flavor.

6337.name: RumChata
6337.note: Cinnamon-horchata cream liqueur. Sweet and easy — a crowd favorite at parties.

6493.name: Luxardo Amaretto
6493.note: A more almond-forward amaretto than Disaronno. Worth trying if you like the style.

6560.name: Kraken Black Spiced Rum
6560.note: Black, thick, cinnamon-forward. Great in a dark cocktail, a bit much on its own.

6659.name: Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
6659.note: The benchmark sweet vermouth. Vanilla and bitter orange — it makes a manhattan.

6733.name: Tres Agaves Blanco
6733.note: Organic and clean. Made for margaritas.

6791.name: Smirnoff Green Apple
6791.note: Sour apple candy flavor, a fine mixer.

6800.name: Montenegro Amaro
6800.note: Balanced, citrus-and-herb Italian amaro. One of the most approachable amari for someone new to the category.

6827.name: Reservoir Rye Whiskey
6827.note: Richmond's own craft rye. Solid, worth it for the Virginia flag.

6860.name: Punt E Mes Vermouth
6860.note: Sweet vermouth with a bitter edge. Terrific in a negroni.

6864.name: IL Tramonto Limoncello
6864.note: A fair mid-tier limoncello. Bright but less complex than the Pallini or Fabrizia versions.

6955.name: Exotico Blanco 100% Agave Tequila
6955.note: Twenty dollars for 100% agave. The best cheap tequila here.

7164.name: Combier Liqueur D'Orange
7164.note: A good, cheaper stand-in for Cointreau.

7165.name: Effen Cucumber Vodka
7165.note: Refreshing and clean, a good mixer for a vodka soda.

7195.name: Twisted Shotz Sex On The Beach
7195.note: A pre-mixed party shot. Sweet and one-note, exactly what the format promises.

7315.name: 99 Whipped Cream
7315.note: Cake-batter sweet. Better poured over dessert than drunk neat.

7351.name: New Amsterdam Vodka
7351.note: Harsh. There are better options two dollars up.

7352.name: Corzo Anejo
7352.note: A fine, unremarkable anejo. Nothing wrong with it, nothing that stands out either.

7355.name: Wild Turkey 81
7355.note: The softer Wild Turkey. Perfectly good; the 101 is better for five dollars more.

7373.name: Crop Harvest Earth  Organic Artisanal Vodka
7373.note: Clean, certified-organic vodka. Solid everyday choice for the eco-conscious shopper.

7376.name: Twisted Shotz Buttery Nipple
7376.note: Butterscotch-cream shot, similar tier to the schnapps-based original.

7383.name: Twisted Shotz B52
7383.note: Coffee-cream-orange shot, does the classic layered drink in one pour.

7393.name: Caribou Crossing SB Canadian
7393.note: Rare single-barrel Canadian whisky. More character than any blend on this shelf.

7450.name: Remy Martin VSOP
7450.note: Rounder and richer than VS cognacs. Good value at its tier.

7479.name: Johnnie Walker Double Black
7479.note: Smokier and more intense than standard Black Label -- a fair step up for the modest price difference.

7507.name: High West Double Rye
7507.note: A blend of young and old rye. Peppery, complex for thirty dollars.

7514.name: Linie Aquavit
7514.note: Norwegian caraway spirit, aged at sea. Distinctive and worth trying if you like herbal spirits.

7520.name: Smirnoff Whipped Cream Vodka
7520.note: Cake-batter sweet. Built for a dessert shot, not much else.

7660.name: Knob Creek Rye
7660.note: 100 proof, same house style as Knob Creek Bourbon. Bold and a genuine step up in this price range.

7761.name: Pallini Limoncello
7761.note: One of the better widely-available limoncellos. Bright, real lemon character.

7797.name: No. 3 London Dry Gin
7797.note: Berry Bros bottling. Six botanicals, nothing wasted, textbook London dry.

7876.name: Pennsylvania Dutch Pumpkin Cream Liqueur
7876.note: Seasonal pumpkin spice cream, sweet and appropriately autumnal.

7878.name: Skinnygirl White Peach Margarita
7878.note: Lower-calorie marketing, but the flavor is thin compared to a real tequila margarita.

7911.name: Jefferson's Rye
7911.note: Canadian-sourced, blended for smoothness rather than rye spice. Approachable if Bulleit is too sharp.

7913.name: Old Parr 12yr Scotch
7913.note: A well-aged blend, popular in export markets. Smooth and easy-drinking.

7981.name: Cardenal Mendoza Black Carton
7981.note: Spanish brandy de Jerez, aged in sherry casks. One of the best brandies in the store outside of cognac.

7995.name: Crater Lake Vodka
7995.note: Oregon craft vodka, smooth and reliable.

7999.name: Masterson's 10yr Straight Rye Whiskey
7999.note: Canadian-sourced, well-aged. Consistently one of the better-reviewed ryes at this price.

8296.name: Firefly Cherry Moonshine
8296.note: Sweet cherry, similar tier to the other mass-market fruit shines.

8297.name: Firefly White Lightning Moonshine
8297.note: From the sweet-tea vodka people. A basic unflavored moonshine, nothing special.

8317.name: Templeton Rye
8317.note: Good whiskey wrapped in a fictional Prohibition story. Priced for the story.

8337.name: Larceny Bourbon
8337.note: Wheated and easy-drinking. A gentler cousin to Weller.

8390.name: Noilly Prat Extra Dry Vermouth
8390.note: Rich for a dry vermouth and only fourteen dollars. Very good in a martini.

8419.name: St. Elder Natural Elderflower Liqueur
8419.note: Comparable to Fiorente -- a genuinely good, affordable elderflower liqueur.

8468.name: Novo Fogo Silver Cachaca
8468.note: Organic Brazilian cachaca, grassy and vegetal. The real base for an authentic caipirinha.

8509.name: Aviation Gin
8509.note: Soft, lavender-and-sarsaparilla, juniper way in the back. Good in sours.

8577.name: Luxardo Maraschino
8577.note: Funky, nutty cherry. Essential for a last word or an aviation.

8600.name: Casamigos Tequila Blanco
8600.note: Smooth and sweet. Forty-five dollars is celebrity pricing.

8714.name: Talisker Storm
8714.note: More smoke and pepper than the 10, no age statement. Good value.

8741.name: Mary Hite Bowman Caramel Cream
8741.note: A Virginia-made caramel cream liqueur. Smooth and well-balanced.

8851.name: 2 Gingers Irish Whiskey
8851.note: Straightforward and easy-drinking, a fine mixer or shot.

8905.name: Crown Royal XO
8905.note: Cognac-cask finished. Fruitier and richer than Reserve — pick whichever finish you prefer.

8978.name: Jefferson's Ocean - Aged At Sea
8978.note: The gimmick (aged on a ship, no two batches alike) is real, and the result is genuinely good.

9007.name: Bols Elderflower Liqueur
9007.note: A cheaper elderflower liqueur than St-Germain. Good enough for a spritz.

9025.name: Ron Barcelo Imperial
9025.note: Dominican, smooth and balanced. A dependable mid-tier aged rum.

9067.name: Jose Cuervo Especial Silver Tequila
9067.note: Mixto. Buy Tradicional for three dollars more.

9074.name: Svedka Mango Pineapple Vodka
9074.note: Tropical fruit flavor, straightforward and sweet.

9075.name: Svedka Strawberry Lemonade Vodka
9075.note: Sweet and tart, a fine warm-weather mixer.

9124.name: Georgia Moon Fruit Jar 100 Proof
9124.note: Higher-proof version of the standard Georgia Moon, sold in the mason-jar bottle.

9143.name: Jose Cuervo La Reserva Platino
9143.note: Cuervo's premium silver. A real step up from the standard bottle, if not a match for the artisanal brands here.

9157.name: Bulldog Gin
9157.note: Smooth and a bit anonymous. Poppy and dragon eye don't announce themselves.

9190.name: Teeling Small Batch Irish Whiskey
9190.note: Rum-cask finished, one of the best-regarded modern Irish blends. Distinctive and well-balanced.

9226.name: Deep Eddy Cranberry Vodka
9226.note: Tart and real-tasting, one of the better flavored vodkas in this price range.

9263.name: The Botanist Islay Dry Gin
9263.note: Twenty-two Islay botanicals, layered and herbal. The most interesting bottle under thirty.

9303.name: Maker's Mark 46 Bourbon
9303.note: Standard Maker's finished with seared French oak staves. More vanilla and spice, worth the upgrade.

9352.name: Ciroc Vodka
9352.note: Made from grapes, not grain — noticeably different texture. Popular for a reason beyond the marketing.

9433.name: Catoctin Creek 1757 Virginia Brandy
9433.note: A Virginia-distilled brandy. Distinctive and worth a look for that alone.

9438.name: Disaronno Amaretto
9438.note: Almond and marzipan. Better than the cheap amarettos by a distance.

9443.name: Basilica Sambuca
9443.note: A solid, mid-tier sambuca. Sweet anise, works well over espresso beans.

9444.name: Romana Sambuca
9444.note: Classic anise liqueur. Sweet, licorice-forward, best iced or in coffee.

9445.name: Gran Gala Triple Orange
9445.note: A cognac-based orange liqueur, richer than a standard triple sec.

9474.name: Jose Cuervo Especial Gold Tequila
9474.note: Mixto with caramel colour. The margarita hangover bottle.

9489.name: Rhum Barbancourt 3 Star
9489.note: Haitian rhum agricole made from fresh cane juice, not molasses -- a distinctly different, grassier profile.

9491.name: Fighting Cock 103
9491.note: 103 proof and unsubtle. Cheap heat, some charm.

9583.name: Tippy Cow Orange Cream Rum
9583.note: Creamsicle flavor on a rum cream base. Sweet and easy.

9584.name: Tippy Cow Vanilla Soft Serve Rum
9584.note: Tastes like soft-serve ice cream, as advertised. A dessert pour.

9615.name: Espolon Anejo
9615.note: Espolòn with real barrel time. Good value añejo.

9845.name: Michter's Us1 Single Barrel Straight Rye
9845.note: Michter's reliable single-barrel program, applied to rye. Smooth for a rye at this proof.

10277.name: Grind Espresso Shot
10277.note: A genuine espresso-forward shot, less sweet than Kahlua. Good for an espresso martini.

10324.name: Senator's Club Whiskey (plastic)
10324.note: As basic as it gets. Buy it for the price.

10342.name: Jose Cuervo Lime Margaritas (plastic)
10342.note: The party-size jug version. Same flavor profile as the glass bottle, cheaper by volume.

10350.name: Seagram's Extra Dry Gin (plastic)
10350.note: Same gin, plastic bottle. Buy it for the cooler, not the bar cart.

10364.name: Jim Beam (plastic)
10364.note: White label in plastic. Mixing only.

10368.name: Smirnoff Vodka 80 Proof (plastic)
10368.note: The plastic-jug version of the standard bottle. Same thin, clean profile, cheaper by volume.

10398.name: Paul Masson Grande Amber VS Brandy
10398.note: Sweet. Everywhere for a reason that is not quality.

10401.name: El Dorado Special Reserve 15 Year Rum
10401.note: One of the best rums in the store at any price. Deep, complex, worth the splurge.

10402.name: Pyrat Reserve XO Rum
10402.note: Orange-forward and sweet. Divisive — great in a punch, odd on its own.

10404.name: Ron Matusalem Gran Reserva 15 Year Rum
10404.note: A genuinely aged sipping rum with real depth. Good value for a stated 15-year age.

10421.name: Midnight Moon Apple Pie Moonshine
10421.note: Ole Smoky's Apple Pie has more name recognition, but this one is just as good and often cheaper.

10423.name: Midnight Moon Strawberry Moonshine
10423.note: Straightforward strawberry, similar tier to the Ole Smoky equivalent.

10424.name: Midnight Moon Blackberry Moonshine
10424.note: Solid blackberry flavor on Midnight Moon's cleaner base.

10427.name: Midnight Moon Moonshine 100 Proof
10427.note: Junior Johnson's unflavored shine, quadruple-distilled. Smoother than Ole Smoky's Original.

10433.name: Georgia Moon Peach Moonshine
10433.note: Georgia Moon's flavored entry. Fine, but the unflavored corn whiskey is the more interesting bottle.

10435.name: Virginia Lightning Apple Pie Moonshine
10435.note: A fair budget alternative to Ole Smoky or Midnight Moon's apple pie.

10451.name: Seagram's 7 Crown Whiskey
10451.note: Thin and sweet. A 7-and-7 and nothing else.

10455.name: High West Whiskey Rendezvous Rye
10455.note: A blend of two straight ryes, one young and spicy, one older and rounder. Well-balanced, well-regarded.

10464.name: Seagram's Lime Twisted Gin
10464.note: Candied lime. Does the work of a gin and a mixer, badly.

10465.name: Tanqueray Rangpur Gin
10465.note: Rangpur lime built in. Genuinely good in a gin and tonic.

10473.name: Grey Goose L'orange Vodka
10473.note: Grey Goose's clean French wheat base with real orange character. A cut above most flavored vodkas.

10482.name: Pinnacle Whipped Vodka
10482.note: Cake-frosting sweet. A novelty flavor for dessert shots.

10488.name: Skyy Infusions Citrus Vodka
10488.note: A clean, well-made citrus vodka, a step above the budget flavored brands.

10490.name: Smirnoff Strawberry Vodka
10490.note: Sweet strawberry candy flavor, unremarkable but reliable.

10526.name: Ketel One Citroen Vodka
10526.note: One of the better citrus vodkas available -- Ketel One's quality base makes a real difference.

10535.name: Three Olives Citrus Vodka
10535.note: Basic citrus flavor, comparable to the Smirnoff equivalent.

10541.name: Three Olives Triple Shot Espresso Vodka
10541.note: Genuinely useful for an espresso martini in a pinch, real coffee flavor.

10546.name: Ketel One Oranje Vodka
10546.note: Real orange character on an excellent base spirit.

10566.name: Pinnacle Salted Caramel Vodka
10566.note: Sweet caramel, fine in a spiked coffee or dessert cocktail.

10579.name: Seagram's Extra Dry Gin
10579.note: Rested in oak, faintly sweet. Fine in a tall drink, dull in a martini.

10581.name: Bombay Dry Gin
10581.note: The original, not Sapphire. More juniper, less perfume, seven dollars cheaper.

10585.name: Mount Gay Eclipse Rum
10585.note: Barbados's everyday rum. Balanced and well-made for twenty-two dollars.

10589.name: Bacardi Gold Rum
10589.note: Slightly rounder than Superior. Not worth seeking out over it.

10593.name: Bacardi Superior Rum
10593.note: The default well rum for a reason. Clean, neutral, forgettable — exactly what a mojito wants.

10605.name: Jim Beam Black
10605.note: Older, rounder Beam. The white label with the corners sanded off.

10608.name: Jim Beam Single Barrel Bourbon
10608.note: A real step up from standard Beam — single barrel, more character, still a fair price.

10619.name: Stolichnaya Vodka
10619.note: Crisp and grainy. Good in a bloody mary.

10629.name: Ketel One Vodka
10629.note: Clean and faintly citrus. The best of the big names.

10664.name: Angel's Envy Rye Whiskey
10664.note: Finished in rum casks (varies by batch). Distinctive and well-reviewed, a departure from a straight rye profile.

10708.name: Aberlour A'bunadh Single Malt Scotch
10708.note: Cask strength, no chill filtration, batch-varying. A cult favorite among Speyside drinkers.

10709.name: Aberlour 12 Year Single Malt Scotch
10709.note: A well-balanced sherry-and-bourbon-cask Speyside. Consistently well-reviewed.

10710.name: Aberlour 16 Year Single Malt Scotch
10710.note: More depth and age than the 12 Year, a genuine step up.

10714.name: Bunnahabhain 12 Year Single Malt Scotch
10714.note: One of the least peated Islay malts -- sherry-forward and approachable if you find the others too smoky.

10718.name: Chivas Regal 18 Year Scotch
10718.note: A well-regarded premium blend, richer and more complex than the standard 12 Year.

10721.name: Dewar's Special Reserve 12 Year Scotch
10721.note: A real step up from White Label. Decent value.

10723.name: Glendronach 12 Year Single Malt Scotch
10723.note: A rich, sherry-forward Speyside. Consistently well-reviewed among sherry-cask fans.

10729.name: Gordon's Vodka 80 Proof
10729.note: Basic well vodka. Fine in a Bloody Mary, nowhere else.

10758.name: Pusser's British Navy Rum
10758.note: The historic Royal Navy rum recipe. Rich, full-bodied, genuinely distinctive among dark rums.

10844.name: 1792 Sweet Wheat Bourbon
10844.note: Wheated variant of 1792. Softer and rounder than the rye-forward flagship.

10851.name: Hell Cat Maggie Irish Whiskey
10851.note: A decent budget-tier blend, unremarkable but fine for mixing.

10999.name: The Quiet Man Traditional Irish Whiskey
10999.note: A solid, traditional-style blend. Unremarkable but competent.

11088.name: Filibuster Boondoggler
11088.note: Virginia-distilled blend, light and easy. A local curiosity more than a standout.

11096.name: Kopper Kettle Golden Gin
11096.note: Virginia, oak-rested. Try it where you'd use a light whiskey.

11106.name: Olmeca Altos Reposado
11106.note: Same quality, a little rounder. Excellent value.

11111.name: Deep Eddy Peach Vodka
11111.note: Solid peach flavor, consistent with the Deep Eddy quality tier.

11202.name: Vitae Spirits Platinum Rum
11202.note: Charlottesville craft rum. Clean and competent.

11326.name: Cabo Wabo Tequila Blanco
11326.note: Fine. Nothing about it justifies the shelf position.

11329.name: Balvenie 12 Year Single Barrel Scotch
11329.note: Single-barrel expression, more variation and character than the Doublewood.

11480.name: Sipsmith Dry London Gin
11480.note: Small-batch, pot-stilled London dry done properly. Excellent balance of juniper and citrus.

11510.name: Jim Beam Double Oak
11510.note: Twice-barreled Beam. More oak, still Beam.

11561.name: Havana Club Anejo Clasico
11561.note: The Bacardi-made 'Havana Club' sold stateside, not the Cuban original. Pleasant, light, unremarkable.

11571.name: Jim Beam Devil's Cut
11571.note: Extra barrel character. A bit hot and hollow.

11572.name: Eagle Rare 10 Year Bourbon
11572.note: Ten years old, Buffalo Trace juice, at a price that has not caught up to the rest of that lineup yet. Buy it while that lasts.

11595.name: Avion Silver Tequila
11595.note: Smooth and inoffensive. You are paying for the bottle.

11603.name: Chambord
11603.note: Rich black raspberry. Sweet, useful in small amounts.

11606.name: Rich & Rare Whisky
11606.note: As basic as Canadian whisky gets. A mixer, nothing more.

11614.name: Copper& Kings American Craft Brandy
11614.note: Kentucky craft brandy, pot-distilled like bourbon. Bold and different from French style.

11629.name: Joseph Magnus Bourbon
11629.note: Finished in cognac, sherry, and pot-still rum casks. Distinctive and well-reviewed, if a bit of a departure from a classic bourbon.

11668.name: Absente Absinthe
11668.note: American-made wormwood absinthe. Real anise punch, milder than the European originals.

11676.name: Di Amore Amaretto
11676.note: A reliable, mid-tier amaretto. Almond-forward without being cloying.

11682.name: Ardbeg 10 Year Islay Single Malt Scotch
11682.note: The peatiest of the approachable Islays, and superb. Not a beginner bottle.

11690.name: Ardbeg Uigeadall Scotch
11690.note: Sherry-cask influence over the peat. Widely considered one of Ardbeg's best standard releases.

11691.name: Aristocrat Southern Style Peach Schnapps
11691.note: Same tier as Aristocrat's other schnapps. A mixer, not a sipper.

11693.name: Auchentosahn American Oak Scotch
11693.note: A light, approachable Highland malt at a fair price.

11706.name: Ballantine's Scotch
11706.note: A reliable, inoffensive budget blend. Smooth and simple, fine for mixing.

11713.name: Barton Peach Schnapks
11713.note: Barton-tier everything: cheap, thin, does the minimum.

11719.name: Benchmark No. 8
11719.note: Thin, but it is thirteen dollars and it is not offensive.

11721.name: Benedictine
11721.note: Honeyed and herbal. Makes a vieux carré.

11734.name: Bluecoat Barrel Finish Gin
11734.note: American gin finished in used bourbon barrels. Vanilla and oak layered over juniper — different, and it works.

11736.name: Bondurant Brother's Moonshine
11736.note: Named for the real Franklin County, VA bootlegging family the movie Lawless was based on. Clean, unflavored, worth trying for the history alone.

11746.name: Buchanan's Deluxe 12 Year Scotch
11746.note: A smooth, well-regarded blend, especially popular in Latin American markets.

11747.name: Buchanan's Deluxe 18 Year Scotch
11747.note: A well-aged premium blend, smoother and richer than the 12 Year.

11749.name: Bulleit Rye Whiskey
11749.note: 95% rye mashbill, spicy and assertive. The rye equivalent of Bulleit Bourbon — a cocktail workhorse.

11757.name: Bushmills Irish Whiskey
11757.note: The standard Bushmills blend. Light, honeyed, a reliable everyday Irish whiskey.

11758.name: Bushmills Black Bush Irish Whiskey
11758.note: Sherry-heavy and smooth. Better than the white label.

11782.name: Caol Ila 12 Year Scotch
11782.note: Lighter and more maritime than Laphroaig or Ardbeg. A great introduction to Islay for the peat-curious.

11797.name: Castillo White Rum
11797.note: Bottom-shelf white rum. The only argument for it is the price.

11801.name: Cazadores Tequila Blanco
11801.note: Reliable and everywhere. Fine in a margarita.

11818.name: Ciroc Apple Vodka
11818.note: Grape-based Ciroc gives this a slightly different mouthfeel than grain vodkas -- crisp apple flavor.

11819.name: Ciroc Coconut Vodka
11819.note: Real coconut character, useful in a tropical cocktail.

11820.name: Ciroc Peach Vodka
11820.note: Peach flavor on the Ciroc base, smooth and well-balanced.

11821.name: Ciroc Pineapple Vodka
11821.note: Bright pineapple flavor on the smooth grape-based spirit.

11842.name: Courvoisier VSOP Cognac
11842.note: A real step up from VS. Smoother, more dried fruit, worth the extra money.

11854.name: Cruzan Light Rum
11854.note: Interchangeable with Bacardi Superior. Buy whichever's cheaper that week.

11858.name: Cruzan Single Barrel Rum
11858.note: Cruzan's premium single-barrel expression. More depth than their standard flavored line.

11863.name: Dalwhinnie Single Malt Scotch
11863.note: Light, heathery, and delicate -- one of the most approachable Highland malts.

11864.name: Dekuyper Buttershots Schnapps
11864.note: The Buttery Nipple base. Butterscotch is convincing; a shot-bar staple for a reason.

11865.name: Dekuyper Grape Pucker Schnapks
11865.note: Sour grape candy, aggressively so. Does what "Pucker" promises.

11868.name: Dewar's White Label Scotch
11868.note: Soft, cheap, forgettable. A mixing blend.

11891.name: Espolon Tequila Blanco
11891.note: The value benchmark. Peppery, real agave, twenty-eight dollars.

11892.name: Espolon Tequila Reposado
11892.note: Vanilla and oak over Espolon’s good blanco. Great in a margarita.

11896.name: Evan Williams Black
11896.note: The value benchmark under fifteen dollars. Genuinely good for what it costs.

11900.name: Evan Williams Honey
11900.note: Sweet and simple. Fine as a shot, wrong for a cocktail.

11901.name: Evan Williams Peach
11901.note: Peach candy. Mixes with lemonade, if you must.

11903.name: Evan Williams White Label
11903.note: Bottled-in-bond at 100 proof for twenty-one dollars. One of the best deals in the store.

11904.name: Evan Williams Single Barrel Bourbon
11904.note: Vintage-dated single barrels at a Heaven Hill price. Punches well above its cost.

11910.name: Flor De Cana Centenario 12 Year Rum
11910.note: Nicaraguan, well-aged, and consistently well-reviewed. One of the better values in this age range.

11917.name: George Dickel No. 12 Tennessee Whiskey
11917.note: The other Tennessee whiskey. Drier than Jack and better value at twenty-six.

11922.name: George Dickel Rye
11922.note: 95% rye from Indiana, charcoal-filtered in Tennessee. Consistently good.

11925.name: Glenfarclas 10 Year Single Malt Scotch
11925.note: Sherried Speyside, family-owned, underpriced for what it is.

11927.name: Glenfiddich 12 Year Scotch
11927.note: Pear and light oak. The other safe Speyside.

11928.name: Glenfiddich 14 Year Scotch
11928.note: Bourbon-barrel reserve, more depth than the 12 Year at a fair price increase.

11929.name: Glenkinchie 12 Year Scotch
11929.note: A Lowland malt, lighter and grassier than most Highland or Speyside bottles.

11930.name: Glengoyne 10 Year Scotch
11930.note: Unpeated Highland malt, light and grassy. A fair value entry point.

11935.name: Glenmorangie Nectar D'or Scotch
11935.note: Sauternes-cask finished, sweet and distinctive among the Glenmorangie range.

11945.name: Grant's Scotch
11945.note: Similar tier to Ballantine's -- a fair everyday mixing blend.

11946.name: Green Spot Irish Whiskey
11946.note: Pot still, orchard fruit, lively. Excellent.

11951.name: Henry McKenna Bourbon
11951.note: The cheap McKenna, not the 10-year bonded. Thin but honest at thirteen dollars.

11953.name: Henry Mckenna Single Barrel Bourbon
11953.note: Once named World Whisky of the Year at a fraction of what that title usually costs. Still one of the best values in bourbon when you can find it.

11962.name: Hornito's Black Barrel Tequila
11962.note: Aged in charred barrels. Drinks more like whiskey than tequila.

11968.name: Ice 101 Peppermint Schnapps
11968.note: 101 proof peppermint. Strong enough that bartenders actually reach for it.

11974.name: J & B Rare Scotch
11974.note: Light and grain-forward. A basic mixing blend, nothing more.

11978.name: Jack Daniel's Single Barrel Tennessee Whiskey
11978.note: Stronger and oakier than Old No. 7. Worth the jump.

11984.name: Jameson Black Barrel Irish Whiskey
11984.note: Jameson's premium small-batch expression. Richer and more complex than the standard bottle.

11986.name: Jameson Irish Whiskey
11986.note: Smooth, easy, everywhere. Fine — Powers is more interesting.

11993.name: Jim Beam Rye
11993.note: The yellow-label rye. A fine well pour.

11997.name: Johnnie Walker Black Scotch
11997.note: The reliable blend. Smoke, fruit, consistency.

12000.name: Johnnie Walker Green Scotch
12000.note: A blended malt built from four single malts including Talisker and Linkwood. Distinctive among the Walker range.

12002.name: Johnnie Walker Red Scotch
12002.note: Harsh neat, fine in a highball.

12155.name: Virginia Lightning Butterscotch
12155.note: A budget butterscotch shine, fine for the price.

12156.name: Virginia Lightning Peach
12156.note: Straightforward peach, priced well below the Tennessee brands.

12179.name: Vitae Spirits Modern Gin
12179.note: Charlottesville. A well-made modern gin, worth a look if buying Virginia matters to you.

12180.name: Vitae Spirits Golden Rum
12180.note: Vitae's aged expression, a fair step up from their Platinum.

12242.name: Alize Peach
12242.note: Peach variant on the Alize formula, consistent sweetness with the line.

12275.name: Breckenridge Distiller's High Proof Blend
12275.note: High-proof Colorado blend. Spicier and more assertive than most blended whiskey.

12294.name: Deep Eddy Orange Vodka
12294.note: Clean orange flavor, a fair mixer.

12298.name: Brugal 1888 Rum
12298.note: Brugal's premium sherry-cask-finished rum. Smooth and well-regarded, a real step up from their standard line.

12325.name: Kilbeggan Irish Whiskey
12325.note: A genuinely solid budget blend from Ireland's oldest licensed distillery.

12327.name: Knob Creek Bourbon
12327.note: Nine years old, 100 proof, unapologetically oaky. A lot of bourbon for the money.

12347.name: Laphroaig Select Scotch
12347.note: A lighter, more approachable entry into Laphroaig's famously smoky style.

12352.name: Larressingle XO Armagnac
12352.note: Aged armagnac with real rustic depth. Underrated next to XO cognac at a similar price.

12359.name: Lunazul Tequila Blanco
12359.note: Good agave character for the money.

12366.name: Martini & Rossi Extra Dry Vermouth
12366.note: Serviceable. Refrigerate it once open, whatever you buy.

12377.name: Milagro Tequila Reposado
12377.note: Pleasant. The blanco is the better buy.

12378.name: Monkey Shoulder Scotch
12378.note: Blended malt built for cocktails. Genuinely useful.

12485.name: Effen Blood Orange Vodka
12485.note: A Dutch wheat vodka with genuine blood orange flavor. Solid mid-premium option.

12526.name: Papa's Pilar Blonde Rum
12526.note: Hemingway-branded, solar-aged. A fair sipping rum, more marketing than a category standout.

12528.name: Jim Beam Vanilla
12528.note: Vanilla syrup with a whiskey accent.

12534.name: Blue Chair Bay Banana Rum Cream
12534.note: Kenny Chesney's rum cream line. Genuinely good banana flavor, a step up from the bargain creams.

12535.name: Blue Chair Bay Key Lime Rum Cream
12535.note: Tart-and-sweet key lime, one of the better flavored rum creams available.

12654.name: Meletti Amaro
12654.note: Saffron-tinted, herbal and citrusy. Well-balanced Italian amaro.

12685.name: Ezra Brooks Bourbon Cream
12685.note: A real bourbon base gives this more character than most flavored cream liqueurs.

12712.name: 1792 High Rye Whiskey
12712.note: Higher rye content than the flagship 1792, filed here for the mashbill. Spicier, still recognizably 1792.

12713.name: Ancient Age (plastic)
12713.note: Bottom of the Buffalo Trace family tree. Mixer only.

12735.name: El Dorado 5-year Rum
12735.note: Demerara rum's best cheap entry point. Rich, sweet, real depth for twenty-five dollars.

12736.name: El Dorado 3-year Rum
12736.note: Guyanese, from a distillery famous for its aged expressions. Smooth even at this young age.

12925.name: Ole Smoky Mountain Java Moonshine
12925.note: Coffee-flavored, sweet rather than bitter. A dessert-drink base.

12951.name: Patron Extra Anejo
12951.note: More time in oak than the standard Anejo, with real added depth to show for it.

12953.name: Ole Smoky Blackberry Moonshine
12953.note: Solid blackberry flavor, sweeter than a real fruit liqueur.

13003.name: Tomatin Scotch Whisky Dualchas
13003.note: A step up from the 12 Year, more sherry-cask influence.

13017.name: Writers' Tears Copper Pot Irish Whiskey
13017.note: A blend of pot-still and single malt whiskeys. Well-regarded and distinctive.

13079.name: Blackbeard's Point Rum
13079.note: Virginia craft rum, decent and unremarkable.

13083.name: Jameson Caskmates Ipa Irish Whiskey
13083.note: Finished in IPA beer casks -- a genuinely distinctive, hoppy twist on standard Jameson.

13142.name: Canadian Mist Whisky (plastic)
13142.note: Thin and neutral. Fine for a well pour, forgettable everywhere else.

13183.name: Old Overholt Bonded
13183.note: The 100-proof bonded Overholt, not the 80. Far better and only three dollars more.

13255.name: Old Elk Blended Straight Bourbon Whiskey
13255.note: A blend of straight bourbons, not neutral spirit. Smooth and well-reviewed for the price.

13310.name: Bacardi Gran Reserva Diez
13310.note: Ten-year Bacardi done properly. Better than the price suggests.

13348.name: Martell Cordon Bleu
13348.note: A legendary blend, more spice-forward than Hennessy’s XO. Connoisseurs often prefer it.

13421.name: Santa Teresa 1796 Rum
13421.note: Venezuelan solera, dried fruit and baking spice. A well-regarded sipper.

13425.name: Gin Mare
13425.note: Spanish, arbequina olive and rosemary. Savory rather than sweet — built for a dirty martini.

13432.name: Wild Turkey 101 Bourbon
13432.note: 101 proof, big vanilla and char. Punches far above twenty-eight dollars.

13463.name: El Toro Silver Tequila
13463.note: Cheap mixto. Mixing only, and barely.

13485.name: Wheatley Vodka
13485.note: Buffalo Trace's vodka. Clean and well-made, made by people who know what they're doing.

13493.name: 1792 Bottled In Bond Kentucky Straight Bourbon
13493.note: 1792's high-rye recipe at bottled-in-bond proof. More structure than the flagship Small Batch.

13494.name: Bushmills 10 Year Irish Malt Whiskey
13494.note: Bushmills' entry-level age-stated single malt. A genuine step up from the standard blend.

13546.name: Kahlua Coffee Liqueur
13546.note: Sweet coffee. Fine in a white russian, sugary anywhere else.

13552.name: Russell's Reserve Rye
13552.note: Six years old, Wild Turkey pedigree. Well-aged rye at a price that undercuts most of this list.

13569.name: Speyburn 15 Year Single Malt Scotch
13569.note: More depth than the 10 Year, still priced fairly for the age statement.

13576.name: Russell's Reserve Single Barrel Bourbon
13576.note: Wild Turkey's premium single-barrel line. Consistently well-reviewed, a step above their standard bottles.

13583.name: Belle Isle Ruby Red Grapefruit Moonshine
13583.note: Real grapefruit character on a clean base. One of the better flavored shines here.

13597.name: Jack Daniel's Tennessee Rye
13597.note: Softer and sweeter than most rye. Fine, unexciting.

13598.name: Woodford Reserve Kentucky Straight Rye Whiskey
13598.note: Woodford's rye, same polish as the bourbon. Softer spice than Bulleit, more finish.

13601.name: Old Forester 86
13601.note: The everyday Old Forester. Solid, banana-and-oak, nothing to prove.

13604.name: Old Forester Signature 100
13604.note: Bottled at 100 proof and priced like it is not. Best straight-shelf value here.

13607.name: Jack Daniel's Old No. 7 Tennessee Whiskey
13607.note: Charcoal-mellowed and sweet. Consistent, unexciting, everywhere.

13615.name: Seagram's 7 Crown Whiskey (plastic)
13615.note: Same blend as the glass bottle, cheaper plastic. Fine for mixing.

13647.name: Sauza Hornitos Plata Tequila
13647.note: Crisp and peppery. A decent well tequila.

13662.name: Astral Tequila Blanco
13662.note: Clean and grassy for twenty dollars.

13676.name: Corralejo Silver Tequila
13676.note: Distinctive, slightly floral. The tall blue bottle.

13679.name: Dekuyper Hot Damn! Cinnamon Schnapps
13679.note: A Fireball competitor without the whiskey base. Cinnamon-candy hot, does the shot-bar job.

13715.name: 1800 Ultimate Watermelon Margarita
13715.note: Sweet and fruity rather than tequila-forward.

13737.name: Metaxa 5 Stars Greek Brandy
13737.note: Greek brandy blended with wine and botanicals. Sweet and distinct — not trying to be cognac.

13744.name: Denizen Merchant's Reserve 8yr Rum
13744.note: Denizen's aged sipping rum, a step up in complexity from their Vatted Dark blending rum.

13767.name: Belle Isle Blood Orange Moonshine
13767.note: Tart citrus over the clean corn base. Mixes well with soda.

13801.name: Pendleton Canadian Whisky
13801.note: Smooth, mellow, a little sweet. The rodeo-branding whisky, and it holds up.

13816.name: Fiorente Italian Elderflower Liqueur
13816.note: A fair St-Germain alternative at a lower price. Real elderflower character.

13856.name: Hennessy XO Cognac
13856.note: The benchmark XO cognac. Rich, complex, worth the splurge for a special occasion.

13860.name: Leblon Cachaca
13860.note: Brazilian sugarcane spirit, not aged rum. The standard for a proper caipirinha.

13870.name: 99 Oranges Schnapps
13870.note: Orange soda syrup with proof behind it. Shot-bar standard.

13992.name: Jose Cuervo Authentic Pink Lemonade Margarita
13992.note: Tastes more like spiked lemonade than a margarita.

14013.name: 1800 Ultimate Margarita
14013.note: A real tequila base, but the mix leans sweeter than a bar-made margarita.

14060.name: Evan Williams Black (plastic)
14060.note: Same whiskey, plastic bottle. For the cooler, not the cabinet.

14084.name: Roku Gin
14084.note: Japanese, six botanicals including sakura and yuzu. Delicate and floral, a real change of pace.

14159.name: Beefeater London Dry Gin
14159.note: The benchmark. If a recipe says 'gin', it means this. Hard to beat at $22.

14194.name: Wray & Nephew White Overproof Rum
14194.note: 126-proof Jamaican funk. The backbone of serious tiki drinks — don't sip it neat.

14203.name: Wild Turkey 101 (plastic)
14203.note: Same whiskey as the glass bottle. Buy this one and pocket the difference.

14257.name: E H Taylor Jr Barrel Proof Bourbon
14257.note: The top of the Taylor line and one of the most sought-after barrel-proof bourbons available.

14309.name: Proper No. Twelve Irish Whiskey
14309.note: Thin and sweet. Sold on a fighter, not a distillery.

14346.name: Smirnoff Kissed Caramel Vodka
14346.note: Sweet caramel, works in a spiked coffee drink.

14389.name: Amaro Averna
14389.note: Cola and caramel. Very drinkable after dinner.

14412.name: Lagavulin 8 Year Scotch
14412.note: Younger, brighter, sharper smoke. Cheaper than the 16 and not a compromise.

14416.name: Bruichladdich Port Charlotte 10 Year Scotch
14416.note: Bruichladdich's peated line. Well-balanced smoke with real complexity.

14443.name: Schlichte Steinhager Gin
14443.note: German steinhäger — malty, closer to genever than London dry. An oddity worth trying once.

14482.name: Elijah Craig Barrel Proof Bourbon
14482.note: A genuine cult release at a fair price when you can find it. Consistently excellent across batches.

14490.name: Johnnie Walker 18 Year Scotch
14490.note: Rich and well-aged, a genuine step up in complexity from Gold Label Reserve.

14506.name: Dewar's 15 Year Reserve Scotch
14506.note: A well-aged Dewar's blend, smoother than their standard White Label.

14507.name: Craigellachie 13 Year Single Malt Scotch
14507.note: Meaty and sulfury in a way that stands out from typical Speyside -- distinctive and well-regarded.

14540.name: Martini & Rossi Rosso Sweet Vermouth
14540.note: Everywhere and adequate. Noilly Prat costs the same and is better.

14552.name: Bacardi 8 Year Rum
14552.note: A genuine step up from Bacardi's white rums. Oaky and worth the extra fifteen dollars.

14761.name: Bowman's Vodka
14761.note: As cheap as vodka gets. A well pour, nothing more.

14765.name: Nikka From The Barrel
14765.note: Punchy, rich, remarkably complete. The best-value Japanese bottle here.

14823.name: Glendronach 15yr Revival
14823.note: More depth than the 12 Year, a genuine favorite among sherry-cask Speyside drinkers.

14827.name: Haku Vodka
14827.note: Suntory's rice vodka. Silky texture, very clean — a genuinely different style.

14895.name: Del Maguey Chichicapa Mezcal
14895.note: A legendary single-village mezcal. Smoky and complex in a way most mainstream mezcal never gets close to.

14927.name: Ole Smoky Moonshine Pickles
14927.note: Their pickle gimmick. Convincingly briny; a novelty shot, not much more.

15002.name: Don Julio Reposado Private Cask
15002.note: A single-cask pick of a trusted name. Consistent with the quality Don Julio is known for.

15031.name: Bulleit Rye 12 Year
15031.note: A genuine age-stated step up from standard Bulleit Rye. More depth, still recognizably Bulleit.

15033.name: English Harbour 5 Year Rum
15033.note: Antigua, sherry-cask sweetness. Overlooked and worth a look at this price.

15064.name: Georgia Moon Corn Whiskey
15064.note: Heaven Hill's unaged corn whiskey. A real, historically-labeled corn whiskey rather than a novelty flavor line.

15065.name: Elijah Craig Small Batch Bourbon
15065.note: No age statement now, but the barrel selection is still doing real work. Great value in this tier.

15073.name: Alize Gold Passion
15073.note: Vodka-based passion fruit variant, similar sweetness to Red Passion.

15074.name: Ancho Reyes Chile Liqueur
15074.note: Ancho chile liqueur, smoky heat. A genuinely useful cocktail ingredient, not a novelty.

15085.name: Baileys Original Irish Cream
15085.note: The standard cream liqueur everyone knows. Reliable, sweet, exactly what it says on the label.

15092.name: Battle Standard 142 Navy Strength
15092.note: 114 proof Virginia. Punchy, holds its own in a cocktail.

15102.name: Blanton's Single Barrel Bourbon
15102.note: The bottle that started the modern single-barrel craze. Usually allocated -- genuinely excellent when you find it at a fair price.

15117.name: Caorunn Small Batch Scottish Gin
15117.note: Rowan berry and apple, crisp and dry. Excellent with a slice of red apple.

15125.name: Captain Morgan Private Stock Rum
15125.note: Captain Morgan's premium spiced expression, a bit more depth than the standard bottle.

15127.name: Captain Morgan Original Spiced Rum
15127.note: Vanilla-and-caramel spiced rum everyone already knows. Sweet, simple, does the job.

15130.name: Carolans Irish Cream
15130.note: The value alternative to Baileys. Slightly thinner, but a fair stand-in at a lower price.

15135.name: Catoctin Creek Roundstone Rye Whisky
15135.note: Virginia, 100% rye and organic. Smoother than the mashbill suggests — a genuine local standout.

15136.name: Catoctin Creek Watershed Gin
15136.note: Loudoun County rye base, spicy and distinctive. Best Virginia gin here.

15158.name: Del Maguey Vida Mezcal
15158.note: The mezcal to learn on. Smoky but balanced, and it works in cocktails.

15160.name: Diplomatico Reserva Exclusiva Rum
15160.note: Sweet, rich, dessert-in-a-glass. Rum enthusiasts roll their eyes; everyone else loves it.

15161.name: Dog Star Vodka
15161.note: A fair Virginia craft vodka, clean profile.

15178.name: Fabrizia Limoncello
15178.note: A solid limoncello, less well-known than Pallini but comparable quality.

15188.name: Flying Dragon Spiced Rum
15188.note: A fair Virginia-made spiced rum, unremarkable but competent.

15199.name: Hennessy VSOP Privilege
15199.note: Hennessy's mid-tier. Balanced and reliable, the cognac most people actually drink.

15219.name: Kapali De Cafe Coffee Liqueur
15219.note: Bottom-shelf coffee liqueur. Fine as a mixer, not much else.

15220.name: Kentucky Gentleman Whiskey (bourbon & Blend)
15220.note: Bottom-shelf blend. A well pour, not a sipper.

15233.name: Laird's Applejack
15233.note: American apple brandy, blended with grain. A jack rose wants this.

15234.name: Laird's Apple Brandy 100 Proof
15234.note: All apple, 100 proof, twenty-eight dollars. Far better than the Applejack.

15247.name: Mt. Defiance Rum Dark
15247.note: Mt. Defiance's aged expression, more depth than their white.

15259.name: New Amsterdam Lemon Vodka
15259.note: Straightforward lemon flavor, useful in a vodka lemonade.

15265.name: Carolan's Salted Caramel
15265.note: Similar tier to their standard Irish Cream with a caramel twist.

15267.name: Ole Smoky Blue Flame Moonshine
15267.note: 109 proof, unflavored. Harsher and hotter than the standard Original.

15268.name: Ole Smoky Hunch Punch Moonshine
15268.note: Fruit-punch sweetness, built for a party bowl.

15271.name: Ole Smoky Original Moonshine
15271.note: Unaged corn whiskey, sharper than Belle Isle. The base every flavor here starts from.

15273.name: Paddy's Old Irish Whiskey
15273.note: Light and easy, one of the older Irish whiskey brands still on the shelf.

15286.name: Ragged Branch Signature
15286.note: Charlottesville, estate-grown grain. The best of the small Virginia bourbons here.

15292.name: Redbreast 12 Year Irish Whiskey
15292.note: Single pot still, sherried and rich. The best Irish whiskey most people can buy.

15293.name: Redemption Rye
15293.note: Straightforward MGP rye. Reliable in cocktails.

15295.name: Remy Martin 1738 Accord Royal
15295.note: Rich, oaky cognac between VSOP and XO in style. A favorite among cognac drinkers.

15307.name: Speyburn 10 Year Single Malt Scotch
15307.note: One of the better-value age-stated single malts on the shelf. Light and honeyed.

15311.name: Saint Brendan's Superior Irish Cream
15311.note: A solid, unpretentious Irish cream. Comparable to Carolans in the same price tier.

15329.name: Tim Smith Climax Moonshine
15329.note: From the Moonshiners TV personality's own Virginia operation. Solidly made, unflavored corn whiskey.

15332.name: Tinkerman's Gin
15332.note: Bright and busy, as the name promises.

15333.name: Tomatin 12 Year Scotch
15333.note: A light, fruity Highland malt at a fair price. Unremarkable but pleasant.

15340.name: Trial & Error Golden Rum
15340.note: Trial & Error's aged expression, slightly more character than their Silver.

15346.name: Twin Creeks 1st Sugar Moonshine
15346.note: Virginia craft moonshine, clean and straightforward.

15350.name: Virginia Frost Vodka
15350.note: Another Virginia craft entry, clean and competent.

15355.name: Weller C.y.p.b. Bourbon
15355.note: Higher rye content than the rest of the Weller line for a spicier wheater. Well regarded by collectors.

15356.name: Whistlepig Straight Rye Whiskey
15356.note: Whistlepig's flagship 100% rye. Well-regarded, a fair step up from their Piggyback line.

15486.name: Don Q 151
15486.note: 151-proof Puerto Rican overproof for tiki drinks and flaming presentations. Handle carefully.

15490.name: Siesta Key Toasted Coconut Rum
15490.note: Toasted coconut gives it more depth than a straight coconut rum.

15491.name: Siesta Key Spiced Rum
15491.note: Florida-made spiced rum, a solid warm-weather sipper.

15499.name: Yellowstone Select
15499.note: Well-made and a bit overlooked at this price.

15522.name: 1792 Small Batch
15522.note: Rye-forward and peppery. Holds its own in a cocktail.

15531.name: Appleton Estate Signature Blend Rum
15531.note: Real Jamaican pot-still character for well under bourbon money. Excellent value.

15533.name: Bowman Brothers Virginia
15533.note: Made in Fredericksburg from Buffalo Trace distillate. The Virginia one worth buying.

15534.name: George Bowman Rum
15534.note: Virginia craft rum from the Bowman Brothers distillery. Solid, worth trying alongside their bourbon.

15537.name: Barr Hill Gin
15537.note: Vermont, raw honey added after distillation. Soft and rounded, unlike anything else on this list.

15541.name: Belle Isle Premium Honey Habanero Moonshine
15541.note: Real heat behind the honey sweetness. More interesting than most flavored shine.

15542.name: Belle Isle Premium Moonshine
15542.note: Virginia, organic corn, unaged. Cleaner and less harsh than the Tennessee mass brands.

15555.name: Bumbu The Original Rum
15555.note: Vanilla and banana-forward, sweeter and more dessert-like than a classic spiced rum.

15556.name: Busnel Calvados Vieille Reserve VSOP
15556.note: French apple brandy from Normandy. Real orchard character, distinct from grape brandy.

15566.name: Commonwealth Gin
15566.note: Virginia-made, coriander-forward. Good value at seventeen dollars.

15573.name: D'usse VSOP
15573.note: Jay-Z's cognac brand. Smooth and citrusy, genuinely well-made beyond the celebrity tie-in.

15575.name: E H Taylor Jr. Straight Rye Whiskey
15575.note: Part of the well-regarded Taylor lineup. Consistently excellent, bottled in bond.

15585.name: Dos Hombres Mezcal
15585.note: Bryan Cranston and Aaron Paul's mezcal. The celebrity backing aside, it is genuinely well-made and artisanal.

15614.name: Kill Devil Pecan Honey Rum
15614.note: A novelty Southern-flavored rum, sweet and distinctive if not classic.

15615.name: Kinky Blue Liqueur
15615.note: A tropical, brightly-colored party liqueur. Sweet and simple.

15616.name: Kinky Pink Liqueur
15616.note: Similar tier to Kinky Blue -- built for shots more than sipping.

15622.name: Macchu Pisco
15622.note: Well-regarded Peruvian pisco, floral and smooth.

15628.name: Old Mr. Boston Dark Rum
15628.note: Cooking rum. Fine for banana bread, not your glass.

15636.name: Old Forester Rye 100
15636.note: 100 proof, bright and grassy. Excellent value.

15662.name: Reyka Vodka
15662.note: Icelandic, lava-filtered, genuinely smooth for the price.

15668.name: Spirits Of The Blue Ridge Vodka
15668.note: A solid Virginia craft vodka, clean and unremarkable in a good way.

15673.name: The Balvenie 12yr American Oak
15673.note: Honeyed and easy to like. A safe gift that is also genuinely good.

15674.name: The Balvenie 14 Year Caribbean Cask Scotch
15674.note: Rum-cask finished, sweeter and richer than the Doublewood. Well-regarded.

15675.name: The Balvenie Doublewood 12 Year Scotch
15675.note: One of the most approachable and well-regarded entry points into single malt Scotch.

15679.name: The Glenlivet 12 Year Single Malt Scotch
15679.note: The safe Speyside. Pleasant, mild, everywhere.

15680.name: The Glenlivet 14 Year Single Malt Scotch
15680.note: A genuine step up from the Founders Reserve, with real cask complexity.

15693.name: Uncle Val's Botanical Gin
15693.note: Cucumber and lavender. Nice bottle, nice gin, priced like it knows both.

15694.name: Virago Four-port Rum
15694.note: Virago's aged expression, more character than their standard white.

15731.name: District Made Vodka
15731.note: DC-area craft vodka, clean and well-made.

15735.name: Weller Full Proof
15735.note: Bottled at the barrel-entry proof. More intensity than the standard Weller line without losing the wheated softness.

15741.name: Jagermeister Cold Brew Coffee
15741.note: Coffee and the classic 56-herb Jager blend. More interesting than the fruit variants.

15817.name: Casa Dragones Blanco Puro Agave Azul
15817.note: An ultra-premium sipping blanco, smooth enough to drink neat rather than in a mixed drink.

15845.name: Marie Brizard Peach Liqueur
15845.note: A well-made peach liqueur, useful in classic cocktails calling for creme de peche.

15861.name: Ron Del Barrilito 3-star Rum
15861.note: Puerto Rican, made in the sherry-cask solera style. Distinctive among the Caribbean rums here.

15902.name: Virgin Bourbon 101
15902.note: Obscure, 101 proof, eighteen dollars. Worth trying once.

15915.name: Horse Soldier Small Batch Bourbon
15915.note: Veteran-owned, sourced juice. A fine bottle, but the story is doing more work than the whiskey at this price.

15938.name: Rabbit Hole Heigold High Rye
15938.note: Louisville craft, high-rye mashbill. More refined than most in this price band.

15969.name: Ole Smoky Buckeye Moonshine
15969.note: Peanut butter and chocolate. Tastes like the candy, unapologetically.

16005.name: Speyburn 18 Yr Scotch
16005.note: Speyburn's oldest widely available expression. Well-aged and a fair value at this price.

16027.name: E H Taylor Jr Single Barrel Bourbon
16027.note: Part of the well-regarded Taylor lineup. Bottled in bond, consistently excellent.

16043.name: Dashfire Old Fashioned RTD Can
16043.note: Small-format, bar-quality Old Fashioned in a can. Great for one serving without opening a bottle.

16058.name: Laird's 10th Gen Apple Brandy Bottled In Bond 5 Yr
16058.note: Bonded five-year apple brandy. Superb and still under forty.

16081.name: Peerless Small Batch Bourbon
16081.note: Louisville craft distillery with a real pedigree. Consistently well-reviewed since their first releases.

16093.name: The Dead Rabbit Irish Whiskey
16093.note: A blend created with the acclaimed NYC bar of the same name. Well-balanced and cocktail-friendly.

16121.name: Dashfire Fig & Cascara Manhattan RTD Can
16121.note: An unusual, fruit-forward twist on a Manhattan. Worth trying if the standard version bores you.

16136.name: Zu Zubrowka Bison Grass Vodka
16136.note: Polish bison-grass vodka, herbal and distinctive. Actually tastes like something, unlike most of this shelf.

16171.name: Jameson Cold Brew
16171.note: Coffee-infused Jameson. Sweet and easy, works well in a cocktail.

16178.name: Virago Spirits 151 Rum
16178.note: A high-proof Virginia craft rum, built for tiki drinks needing a float.

16206.name: The Copper Can Moscow Mule
16206.note: A solid canned Moscow Mule, real ginger bite rather than just sweet.

16211.name: Bold Rock Copper Mug Mule
16211.note: Fair canned mule, real ginger presence.

16212.name: Bold Rock Bold Fashioned Cocktail
16212.note: A canned Old Fashioned from a cider company -- decent, if lighter-bodied than a whiskey-forward version.

16236.name: Conniption American Dry Gin
16236.note: Durham, NC. Approachable and citrus-forward, a safe crowd-pleaser.

16240.name: Ole Smoky Apple Pie Moonshine
16240.note: Ole Smoky's best-known flavor for a reason — cinnamon and apple actually taste like pie.

16269.name: Belvedere Heritage 176
16269.note: Belvedere's higher-end rye-based bottling. More character than the standard bottle.

16309.name: High West Double Rye Whiskey Barrel Select
16309.note: A single-barrel pick of the well-liked Double Rye blend. Spicier and more intense than the standard bottle.

16329.name: St. George Spirits Absinthe
16329.note: A genuinely well-made craft absinthe. Complex rather than just intensely anise.

16331.name: 360 Georgia Peach Vodka
16331.note: Straightforward peach flavor, fine for the price.

16333.name: 360 Double Chocolate Vodka
16333.note: Genuinely chocolatey, a novelty dessert vodka.

16336.name: 44 North Potato Vodka
16336.note: Idaho potato vodka -- a fuller, creamier mouthfeel than grain vodkas at a similar price.

16338.name: Jim Beam with Highball Glass
16338.note: White label plus a glass. Buy it for the glass.

16343.name: Cape Charles Apple Pie Moonshine
16343.note: Virginia apple pie shine at a premium price — decent, but Ole Smoky and Midnight Moon do it for less.

16344.name: Cape Charles Blackberry Moonshine
16344.note: Same story as their Apple Pie: fine flavor, priced ahead of the category norm.

16346.name: Catoctin Creek Rabble Rouser Rye
16346.note: Virginia craft, cask strength. More intensity than their standard Roundstone Rye.

16376.name: Trial & Error Limoncello
16376.note: A decent limoncello from a smaller producer. Fine for the price.

16379.name: Old Tub
16379.note: Unfiltered bonded Beam. Rougher and more interesting than the white label.

16382.name: 99 Root Beer Schnapps
16382.note: Genuinely tastes like a root beer float. The best of the 99 lineup by a wide margin.

16383.name: 99 Watermelon Schnapps
16383.note: Jolly Rancher in liquid form. Exactly as advertised.

16390.name: Barr Hill Vodka
16390.note: Raw honey vodka from Vermont. Distinctly sweet-edged and different from anything else on this shelf.

16393.name: Battle Standard 142 Barrel Finished
16393.note: Oak-finished. Interesting neat, muddy in a G&T.

16394.name: Battle Standard 142 Gin
16394.note: Virginia craft, competent across the range.

16395.name: Bayou White Rum
16395.note: Same distillery as the Spiced, clean and unaged.

16396.name: Bayou Spiced Rum
16396.note: Louisiana rum, real vanilla-and-spice character rather than generic sweetness.

16403.name: Brockmans Gin
16403.note: Blueberry and blackberry up front, juniper way in back. More liqueur than gin to purists.

16406.name: Teremana Blanco Tequila
16406.note: Perfectly decent. Priced on celebrity, not liquid.

16416.name: American Harvest Organic Vodka
16416.note: Organic wheat vodka, smooth. A reliable mid-tier choice.

16424.name: Civic Vodka
16424.note: Clean and well-made, a solid regional option.

16433.name: Powers Three Swallow Irish Whiskey
16433.note: Powers' entry-level pot-still expression. Spicy and characterful.

16449.name: Sugarlands Shine Pina Colada Moonshine
16449.note: Coconut and pineapple, straightforward tropical flavor.

16453.name: Edinburgh Classic Gin
16453.note: Traditional Scottish dry gin, heather honey among the botanicals. Solid, unshowy.

16456.name: Fords Gin
16456.note: Built by a bartender for cocktails and it shows. Best all-purpose bottle here after Tanqueray.

16462.name: Malfy Con Arancia
16462.note: Sicilian blood orange, quite sweet. Works in a spritz.

16468.name: Ole Smoky Butter Pecan Moonshine Cream
16468.note: One of the better cream flavors in the lineup — actually reads as butter pecan.

16469.name: Ole Smoky Butterscotch Moonshine
16469.note: Convincing butterscotch, sweet enough to work as a dessert shot.

16471.name: Ole Smoky Tennessee Peach Moonshine
16471.note: Their most "Southern" flavor. Peach comes through clearly.

16491.name: Plymouth Navy Strength Gin
16491.note: Plymouth at 57%. More backbone than the standard bottle, still recognizably Plymouth.

16511.name: Ungava Gin
16511.note: Bright yellow, Arctic botanicals. Novel; the novelty wears off.

16543.name: Koloa Hawaiian Mai Tai
16543.note: Made with real Hawaiian rum, a decent bottled Mai Tai.

16546.name: Sugarlands Blueberry Muffin Moonshine
16546.note: Baked-good sweetness rather than straight blueberry. A dessert flavor.

16547.name: Sugarlands Maple Bacon Moonshine
16547.note: Sweet maple dominates; the bacon note is more marketing than flavor.

16548.name: Sugarlands Shine Mark Rogers Peach Moonshine
16548.note: Celebrity-branded peach shine. Genuinely decent flavor behind the marketing.

16549.name: Sugarlands Shine Appalachian Apple Pie Moonshine
16549.note: Their answer to Ole Smoky Apple Pie. Comparable quality, worth it if it is on sale instead.

16550.name: Sugarlands Shine Butterscotch Gold Moonshine
16550.note: Convincing butterscotch, similar tier to the Ole Smoky version.

16567.name: Van Gogh Dutch Chocolate Vodka
16567.note: Rich and genuinely chocolatey, a good dessert-cocktail vodka.

16570.name: Sugarlands Shine Peanut Butter & Jelly Moonshine
16570.note: Novelty flavor that mostly delivers on the concept. A conversation piece more than a regular pour.

16574.name: Sugarlands Shine Blockader Blackberry Moonshine
16574.note: Standard blackberry flavor, unremarkable next to the Belle Isle version.

16576.name: Sugarlands Shine Root Beer Moonshine
16576.note: Decent root beer float flavor, though the 99 Brand version is sharper.

16581.name: Praline Pecan Liqueur
16581.note: Genuinely tastes like pralines. A good after-dinner sipper or coffee addition.

16645.name: Laws Whiskey House Straight Rye
16645.note: Colorado craft, grain-to-glass. Well-regarded among craft rye drinkers.

16686.name: High West Campfire Whiskey
16686.note: A blend of bourbon, rye and scotch — genuinely unusual and well-executed. One of the more interesting bottles here.

16710.name: Appleton Estate 8 Year Old Reserve
16710.note: Excellent value Jamaican. Rich, dried-fruit depth for well under bourbon prices.

16713.name: Thomas Dakin Gin
16713.note: Manchester dry gin revived from an 1800s recipe. Bergamot and orris root, well balanced.

16729.name: Four Roses Private Selection Barrel Strength
16729.note: A single-store barrel pick from Four Roses' ten recipes. Consistently one of the better barrel-proof bourbons on a shelf.

16744.name: Don Ciccio Figli Amaro Delle Sirene
16744.note: A genuine Italian amaro, bittersweet and complex. Worth trying if you only know Fernet or Campari.

16757.name: Luxardo Limoncello
16757.note: A step up in citrus intensity from the cheaper limoncellos.

16762.name: Torres 10 Imperial Reserve Brandy
16762.note: Spanish brandy de Jerez, sherry-cask aged. Real depth for the price.

16775.name: Schoolcrafts Original Wondermint Schnapps Liqueur
16775.note: Virginia-made peppermint schnapps. Regional novelty more than a category leader.

16792.name: 99 Black Cherry Schnapps
16792.note: Shot-bar novelty. One-note cherry candy, nothing to sip.

16833.name: Cuca Fresca Silver Cachaca
16833.note: A solid, more widely available cachaca. Good for caipirinhas without the premium price.

16860.name: Ole Smoky Moonshine Peaches
16860.note: Peach-forward, less spiced than the Tennessee Peach bottle.

16868.name: Ole Smoky Moonshine Cherries
16868.note: Sweet maraschino-adjacent cherry. A dessert pour more than a mixer.

16877.name: Garrison Brothers Texas Straight Small Batch
16877.note: Texas heat ages this fast and hard -- bold and oaky in a way Kentucky bourbons rarely are.

16907.name: Mi Campo Tequila Blanco
16907.note: Rested in wine barrels. Unusual, works.

16947.name: Maker's Mark 101
16947.note: 101 proof Maker's. Same wheated recipe with more punch and more flavor to back it up.

16960.name: Jose Cuervo Sparkling Paloma
16960.note: Grapefruit and soda -- one of the more drinkable things in the Cuervo RTD lineup.

16961.name: Jose Cuervo Sparkling Lime Margarita
16961.note: The carbonation makes it more refreshing than the still bottled version, at least.

16969.name: Avion Reserva 44 Tequila
16969.note: Avion's top-tier gold expression. Smooth and rounded, priced for the premium positioning.

16987.name: Codigo 1530 Blanco Tequila
16987.note: Very clean, very smooth. Priced for the branding, but good.

17024.name: Herradura Ultra Tequila Anejo
17024.note: Herradura's cristalino-style anejo -- charcoal filtered for a smoother, lighter-colored pour.

17036.name: Hanson Of Sonoma Cucumber Vodka
17036.note: Grape-based, organic, California craft. Real cucumber character, refined.

17037.name: Hanson Of Sonoma Meyer Lemon Vodka
17037.note: Bright and genuine Meyer lemon character on their smooth grape base.

17045.name: Hanson Of Sonoma Original Vodka
17045.note: A grape-based vodka distilled from their own wine grapes -- distinctly smooth mouthfeel.

17055.name: Maestro Dobel Silver Tequila
17055.note: Polished and mild. Easy to drink neat.

17063.name: Olmeca Altos Tequila Plata
17063.note: Built with bartenders for margaritas. Hard to beat at twenty-five.

17078.name: Ron Abuelo Anejo 7 Yr Rum
17078.note: Panamanian, well-aged and balanced. One of the better values in aged rum at this price.

17084.name: Tequila Ocho Anejo
17084.note: Single-estate, vintage-dated agave. Highly regarded among people who take tequila seriously.

17098.name: Ilegal Mezcal Joven
17098.note: Clean and bright for a joven. Good introduction.

17144.name: Tanqueray Sevilla Orange
17144.note: Orange Tanqueray. Better than most flavored gins, still a sidestep.

17171.name: Bumbu XO Rum
17171.note: Heavily sweetened and spiced — closer to a rum liqueur than a rum. Great bottle design, polarizing juice.

17173.name: Don Q Oak Barrel Spiced Rum
17173.note: Puerto Rican, oak-aged before spicing -- a bit more depth than the mass-market spiced brands.

17177.name: El Dorado 12 Year Rum
17177.note: Rich Demerara rum, real complexity. Punches well above its price.

17179.name: El Dorado 8 Year Rum
17179.note: One of the most acclaimed aged rums at this price. Rich, complex, and a genuine step up from the 3 Year.

17184.name: Kill Devil Silver Rum
17184.note: A clean, well-made white rum from a smaller regional distillery.

17196.name: Eight Shires Warrick Silver Rum
17196.note: A clean, unaged Virginia craft rum.

17200.name: Eight Shires Accomac Spiced Rum
17200.note: Virginia craft spiced rum. Warm spice notes, decent alternative to Captain Morgan.

17204.name: Select Aperitivo Pilla
17204.note: Venetian aperitivo, similar lane to Aperol but earthier.

17234.name: Don Q Reserva 7
17234.note: Underrated Puerto Rican sipper. Smooth for the price, quietly good.

17235.name: Evan Williams 1783 Small Batch
17235.note: A real step up from Evan Williams Black for nine more dollars.

17251.name: Selvarey White Rum
17251.note: Panamanian, clean and versatile. Fine for mixing.

17252.name: Smith & Cross Jamaica Rum
17252.note: High-ester pot-still Jamaican, funky and intense. Essential for tiki, too much to sip neat.

17256.name: Trial & Error Silver Rum
17256.note: A basic Virginia craft white rum. Fine for mixing.

17258.name: Mt. Defiance White Rum
17258.note: Virginia craft white rum, clean and functional.

17284.name: Aberfeldy 12 Year Scotch
17284.note: Honeyed and approachable, the backbone of the Dewar's blends bottled on its own.

17295.name: Creek Water Whiskey
17295.note: 100 proof and rough. More attitude than whiskey.

17303.name: Kamiki Blended Japanese Whisky
17303.note: Finished with a touch of sake and umeshu influence. Distinctive, though the flavor is more novelty than classic whisky.

17304.name: Kilchoman Machir Bay Scotch
17304.note: Young but well-made farm-distillery Islay. Smoky and coastal.

17308.name: Virginia Lightning Moonshine 90 Proof
17308.note: A real Virginia corn whiskey, not just a flavored novelty label. Honest and unpretentious.

17309.name: Virginia Lightning Moonshine 100 Proof
17309.note: Same lineage as the 90 proof, more heat. Good value for an actual Virginia-distilled shine.

17320.name: Jameson Caskmates Stout Irish Whiskey
17320.note: Finished in stout casks, richer and more distinctive than the IPA version.

17321.name: Thrashers Spiced Rum
17321.note: A boardwalk-branded spiced rum. Fine, unremarkable.

17323.name: Thrashers White Rum
17323.note: A clean mixing rum from the same line as their Spiced.

17324.name: Thrashers Coconut Rum
17324.note: Sweet coconut flavor, built for a beach drink.

17333.name: Kaiyo The Single 7 Year Whisky
17333.note: Mizunara-cask finished single malt. Distinctive sandalwood-and-coconut character from the Japanese oak.

17334.name: Kaiyo Whisky
17334.note: Kaiyo's standard bottling. The mizunara oak character comes through clearly.

17335.name: Kaiyo Cask Strength Whisky
17335.note: Kaiyo's mizunara character at full proof. More intense and structured than their standard bottling.

17339.name: Leadslingers Napalm Cinnamon
17339.note: Cinnamon, aggressively. Not a sipping decision.

17370.name: Crown Royal Black Whisky
17370.note: Higher proof Crown. More body, still sweet.

17371.name: Crown Royal Whisky
17371.note: The default Canadian whisky. Soft and easy — inoffensive rather than exciting.

17387.name: Ole Smoky Dill Pickle Moonshine
17387.note: Their bulk-size pickle shine. Same gimmick as the standard bottle, bigger jug.

17401.name: St. Remy Authentic XO
17401.note: French brandy, caramel-sweet. Decent for the price, not real cognac.

17408.name: Elijah Craig Straight Rye
